body:
This occurred again in slightly different circumstances, following the (unsuccessful) use of the shard recovery tool. Master logs spam-reported the following error:
```
Caused by: java.nio.file.AccessDeniedException: /data2_encrypted/elasticsearch/nodes/0/indices/_r6I4_5LR8Wf-d1J3g6c-A/0/_state/state-2.st
    at sun.nio.fs.UnixException.translateToIOException(UnixException.java:90) ~[?:?]
```
@nerophon can you post the full stack trace? At first glance it looks like a different (but still valid!) bug

@romseygeek 
The main stack trace is:
```
 [2020-11-13T14:37:16,273][ERROR][o.e.b.ElasticsearchUncaughtExceptionHandler] [hostname_redacted] fatal error in thread [hostname_redacted][masterService#updateTask][T#1]], exiting
 java.lang.StackOverflowError: null
     at java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableCollection$1.<init>(Collections.java:1046) ~[?:?]
     at java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableCollection.iterator(Collections.java:1045) ~[?:?]
...
```
That's how I associated the problem with this bug, apologies if I did so in error. The short trace posted above is just the underlying cause, which AFAIK was due to the shard recovery tool changing a file permission. The whole problem went away once the permission was fixed manually.

Is there any more than that? It would be most useful to get lines that include `org.elasticsearch.*` as that tells us where the problems are within code that we control.  I realise that it might be difficult to get if the problem has gone away now though.
